sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — was one of the smallest stegosaurs, measuring less than four meters in length despite being an adult.
A skeleton model in the Chongqing Municipal museum depicts the animal with fourteen pairs of plates that transformed into spikes towards the tail.
Gregory S. Paul described the unique tail spike arrangement of Chungkingosaurus as a "pin-cushion array".
Chungkingosaurus was a herbivore, like all stegosaurs.
Chungkingosaurus belongs to the class Ornithischia and its parent group is Stegosauridae.

Chungkingosaurus is a stegosaurian dinosaur from the Late Jurassic Upper Shaximiao Formation in modern-day China, living during the Late Jurassic Oxfordian stage, approximately 156 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
Other sources indicate the creature lived during the Bathonian to Callovian stages, from 168.2 to 161.5 million years ago.
Gregory S. Paul suggested in 2010 that Chungkingosaurus was the juvenile form of Tuojiangosaurus.
